solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Shoot that's dangerous when unprotected

definitions.meaning: to shoot is to start firing guns, the order given to troops
a fireplace with an unguarded blaze, risky without a fireguard in front of it

explanation.surface: A warning that some shot or activity is hazardous without protection.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a hearth fire left without a guard, which can spit sparks into the room.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both the command to start shooting and a domestic hearth blaze, so it fits both readings.

clue.text: Pull up, say, dandelion regularly when one droops?

indicators.note: in a down clue, pulling something up reads its letters from the bottom upwards, a reversal

parts.note: EG, short for exempli gratia, stands for 'say' or 'for example'

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word dandelion

explanation.surface: A gardener told to pull up a dandelion at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull up' reverses EG plus ADLO (the even letters of dandelion), giving the two words read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Later life is when the body sags and wilts, a whimsical description of being elderly, marked by the question mark.

clue.text: Permit England manager once to omit wings?

indicators.note: the wings of a word are its outer letters, here dropped from the surname at both ends

parts.note: Terry Venables managed the England football team from 1994 to 1996

explanation.surface: Asking whether a former England football manager may leave out his wingers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to omit wings' strips the first and last letters, V and S, from the manager's surname.
explanation.definitionFit: To permit something is to allow or make it possible, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Fellow at unfinished end of church offers little hope

indicators.note: unfinished means the final letter of the word is cut off

parts.note: the chancel is the eastern end of a church, near the altar

explanation.surface: A man at a half-built church end has little hope to offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unfinished' removes the last letter, L, from the church's end section.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom is sarcastic, meaning there is no realistic prospect at all, so it means little hope.

clue.text: Survey trick during restoration?

indicators.note: during means the one piece sits within the other's span of letters

parts.note: a renaissance is a revival or restoration of something
a con is a trick or swindle

explanation.surface: A building survey with some deceit going on while restoration work happens.
explanation.definitionFit: A military or exploratory survey of ground or a situation is called by this word, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: The Spanish fly recalled complication

indicators.note: recalled is read as called back, so the letters run in the opposite direction

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for 'the'
a gnat is a small flying insect

explanation.surface: Spanish fly, an aphrodisiac, being withdrawn from sale causes problems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recalled' turns ELGNAT round. Spanish fly is a supposed aphrodisiac, but here 'The Spanish' and 'fly' are separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A complication is a knotty, confusing muddle, which is a synonym in the figurative sense.

clue.text: Drier and finer? Take top off

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is removed

parts.note: fairer means finer, as weather that is fair is fine

explanation.surface: Is the weather drier and finer? Then remove a layer of clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take top off' drops F, the first letter of the synonym for finer.
explanation.definitionFit: A clothes horse or rack for laundry is a device for drying, so it is literally a drier.

clue.text: Band hero's a bundle of nerves

parts.note: a gang is a band of people
a lion is a brave or celebrated person, a hero

explanation.surface: The hero of a music group is a nervous wreck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a bundle of nerves' looks like a description of anxiety, but it is meant anatomically.
explanation.definitionFit: In anatomy this is a cluster of nerve cells, literally a knot of nerve tissue.

clue.text: Lamb for one lives in English street

indicators.note: in means these words sit inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: say means for one, as in giving an example
is means lives or exists

explanation.surface: A lamb, for example, living on a street in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lamb' is not the animal: Charles Lamb wrote the Essays of Elia. 'for one' looks like part of the definition but gives SAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Charles Lamb was a celebrated English writer of short prose pieces, so he is an example of the answer.

clue.text: IT worker got out of last nasty mess with happy ending

indicators.note: got out of suggests the letters are extracted and reassembled into a new order
ending picks the final letter of happy

explanation.surface: A computer worker escaped a horrible recent mess and things ended well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got out of' rearranges LASTNASTYMESS together with Y, the last letter of happy.
explanation.definitionFit: This job designs and analyses computer setups for businesses, so the holder works in information technology.

clue.text: Desperate GP with a reduced staff

parts.note: a GP, general practitioner, is a doctor, abbreviated DR

indicators.note: reduced means shortened by its last letter

parts.note: a staff is a walking stick

explanation.surface: A family doctor's surgery is in a desperate state with staff cuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reduced' cuts the final K from STICK. A GP is a British family doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Desperate measures are extreme or severe ones, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Yankee overlooks what guards the crown jewels

parts.note: Yankee is Y in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a building that fronts a view overlooks it

explanation.surface: An American looks over the guard protecting the Crown Jewels in the Tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crown jewels' is slang for a man's genitals, not the royal regalia in the Tower of London; the answer is a style of men's underpants.
explanation.definitionFit: Men's briefs cover and protect the groin, jokingly called the family jewels, hence the comic description.

clue.text: Pull over leading pair in Cheddar Gorge

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the letters are written in reverse

parts.note: to lug is to pull or haul something heavy

indicators.note: the leading pair are the first two letters of the word Cheddar

explanation.surface: Pulling over in Cheddar Gorge, the Somerset beauty spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Cheddar Gorge is a limestone ravine in Somerset, England; here 'Cheddar' gives only its first two letters and 'Gorge' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep narrow ravine in the American West is called this, so it is a synonym for gorge.

clue.text: Do a turn with supporter of course

indicators.note: to do something over is to reorganise it, so the following letters are rearranged

parts.note: an ally is a supporter

explanation.surface: A performer does a turn on stage with a backer, as expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' rearranges ATURN to NATUR; 'a turn' looks like a stage act.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Of course' and the answer both mean as might be expected, interchangeable adverbs.

clue.text: Damage bulb mostly in US housing that's not compatible

indicators.note: housing means the outer words enclose the other pieces

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
to harm is to damage

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter is kept

parts.note: an onion is a bulb

explanation.surface: Harm to a bulb in American housing that doesn't fit in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in US' looks like the location, but those two words are the outer shell: 'housing' wraps them round the damage and the shortened bulb ('mostly' drops its last letter).
explanation.definitionFit: Things that clash and do not agree are discordant or ill-matched, which matches not compatible.

clue.text: Superman fan's zest misplaced during recess

definitions.note: the possessive 's here is 'is': the definition is the Superman fan

indicators.note: during means one piece is set within the other

parts.note: a niche is a recess in a wall

indicators.note: misplaced means the letters are put out of their normal order

explanation.surface: A comic-book fan's enthusiasm for Superman put away in an alcove.
explanation.walkthrough: The Superman here is the Übermensch of German philosophy, not the comic hero; 'misplaced' scrambles the zest and 'during' sets it in the recess.
explanation.definitionFit: The German philosopher proposed the Übermensch, usually translated Superman, so he championed that ideal.

clue.text: Motor's way below old scuttled U-boat

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is': the motor is the definition

indicators.note: below in a down clue places the road abbreviation under the rest
a scuttled vessel is wrecked, so its letters are broken up and reordered

parts.note: RD, road, is a way

explanation.surface: A boat's engine is far down below a sunk old German submarine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scuttled' scrambles the submarine's letters and 'below' puts the way at the foot of this down entry; 'Motor's' is the definition plus 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine clamped to the stern of a small boat is known by this name, a kind of motor.

clue.text: Like some porticos, poorly trimmed on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside means the trimmed word wraps around the other

parts.note: pared means trimmed or cut back
poorly means unwell, ill

explanation.surface: Porticos badly trimmed on their exterior.
explanation.definitionFit: Porticos are porches supported by columns, so many are described as having columns.

clue.text: Country cousin at heart

parts.note: the heart of the word cousin is its middle pair of letters, U and S, the initials of a country

explanation.surface: A rural relative who is a country bumpkin at heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Country cousin' suggests a bumpkin, but 'Country' is the definition and the central letters of cousin abbreviate it.
explanation.definitionFit: The middle two letters of cousin are the usual abbreviation for America, a nation.

clue.text: Former Anglicans screen sex for thrill

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: to screen is to shield, so the church abbreviation surrounds the other piece

parts.note: CE is the Church of England, the Anglican church
it is slang for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: Former churchgoers censor sexual content to get a thrill.
explanation.definitionFit: To excite someone is to stir or arouse them, a synonym of thrill as a verb.

clue.text: Having to do with stars from south Universal sacked

indicators.note: sacked means dismissed, so the letter goes out of the word

parts.note: austral means southern, from the south
U is the film classification for universal

explanation.surface: A film studio's star business moved from the south after staff were fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from south' looks like a direction for reading, but it is a synonym; 'sacked' removes U from it.
explanation.definitionFit: Astral describes things relating to the heavens and celestial bodies, matching the definition.

clue.text: Bacall undermined Gardner's battle

indicators.note: undermined means subverted, so the letters of Bacall are rearranged

parts.note: Ava Gardner was a Hollywood film star

explanation.surface: Lauren Bacall sabotaged Ava Gardner's struggle, a Hollywood rivalry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undermined' rearranges BACALL to BALACL. The battle was fought in the Crimean War, 1854.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1854 Crimean War engagement included the Charge of the Light Brigade, so it names a battle.

clue.text: Maybe cramp officer in charge

parts.note: COL is the abbreviation for colonel, an officer

explanation.surface: Perhaps the commanding officer is suffering from a cramp.
explanation.definitionFit: Colic is severe abdominal pain, and cramp is one example of such pain, hence 'Maybe'.

clue.text: Start to Zoom with a Lord's big shot about line on chart

indicators.note: start to means the opening letter of the next word
about means turned round, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: Lord's is the London cricket ground; a big shot clearing the boundary scores six

explanation.surface: A cricketer starts zooming, hitting a big shot at Lord's.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the famous London cricket ground, where a six is a hit over the boundary. 'about' turns SIX round.
explanation.definitionFit: In a three-dimensional graph this is the axis for depth, one of the lines on the chart.

clue.text: Paint girl briefly suppressing sob

indicators.note: suppressing means holding something in, so the shortened name surrounds the other piece
briefly means the name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name
to sob is to cry

explanation.surface: A painting of a girl holding back her sobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paint' opens the clue looking like a verb but is the noun defined; 'briefly' shortens the girl and 'suppressing' holds the sob inside her.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick-drying synthetic emulsion used by artists, so it is a type of paint.

clue.text: Crikey! Fancy storing uniform in worse mess

indicators.note: storing means holding inside, so the rearranged letters surround the other piece
fancy as in fanciful, imaginative, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: Uniform is U in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at a uniform kept in an even messier state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' rearranges CRIKEY to YCKIER and 'storing' puts U in it. 'Crikey' and 'Fancy' both look like exclamations.
explanation.definitionFit: Yucky means messy and nasty, so the comparative describes something in a worse, more disgusting state.

clue.text: Big hack splits channel dock

indicators.note: splits means the other piece cuts into this one, opening it up

parts.note: a duct is a channel for fluid or air
ED, editor, is the top journalist, a big hack

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor divides a waterway at a dock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dock' looks like the noun for ships, but it is the verb meaning to take away.
explanation.definitionFit: To dock wages is to take money off them, so the verb means subtract.

clue.text: Exquisite number on each line

parts.note: read as something that numbs: ether is an anaesthetic

explanation.surface: A beautiful number placed on each line of a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is read as NUMB-er, something that numbs, not a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something delicate and light, almost too perfect for this world, is exquisite in this sense.
